questions.stem: What is the unit of Planck's constant?
questions.solution: Planck's constant has units of joule-seconds (J s) because it relates energy to frequency in the equation E = hf. The unit kg m/s is for momentum, N/m is for spring constant, and W/m² is for power per area, none of which match the units of Planck's constant.

hi.stem: प्लैंक नियतांक का मात्रक क्या है?
hi.solution: प्लैंक नियतांक के मात्रक जूल-सेकंड (जे से) होते हैं क्योंकि यह समीकरण E = hf में ऊर्जा के आवृत्ति से संबंध दर्शाता है। किग्रा मी/से संवेग के मात्रक हैं, एन/मी स्प्रिंग नियतांक के मात्रक हैं, और वॉट/मी² क्षेत्रफल प्रति शक्ति के मात्रक हैं, जो कोई भी प्लैंक नियतांक के मात्रक के साथ मेल नहीं खाते।
hi.critique: Translation is accurate, technical terms are standard in Hindi textbooks, and the question structure matches the original.

questions.stem: What is the unit of energy commonly used in atomic and nuclear physics?
questions.solution: The electron volt is the unit of energy commonly used in atomic and nuclear physics because it is a very small unit that matches the scale of energy involved in atomic processes. The joule is too large for such small-scale energy measurements, the calorie is used in thermodynamics and nutrition, and the kilowatt hour is a unit of electrical energy for larger, practical applications.

hi.stem: परमाणु एवं नाभिकीय भौतिकी में ऊर्जा के इकाई क्या है?
hi.solution: इलेक्ट्रॉन वोल्ट परमाणु एवं नाभिकीय भौतिकी में ऊर्जा की इकाई है क्योंकि यह एक बहुत छोटी इकाई है जो परमाणु प्रक्रियाओं में शामिल ऊर्जा के पैमाने के साथ मेल खाती है। जूल इस छोटे पैमाने की ऊर्जा माप के लिए बहुत बड़ा है, कैलोरी ऊष्मागतिकी एवं पोषण में उपयोग की जाती है, एवं किलोवाट घंटा बड़े व्यावहारिक अनुप्रयोगों के लिए विद्युत ऊर्जा की इकाई है।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses standard scientific terminology as found in Hindi textbooks.

questions.stem: What conclusion did Hallwachs draw from his experiment where a zinc plate lost its charge when illuminated by ultraviolet light?
choices: Electrons were emitted from the zinc plate
Protons were emitted from the zinc plate
Neutrons were emitted from the zinc plate
Ions were emitted from the zinc plate
questions.solution: Hallwachs concluded that electrons were emitted from the zinc plate when illuminated by ultraviolet light, as the loss of charge indicated the release of negatively charged particles. Protons and neutrons are not emitted in this process because they are bound within the nucleus and not involved in the photoelectric effect. Ions are charged atoms, not the elementary particles emitted in this type of experiment.

questions.stem: What is the main factor that determines the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons in the photoelectric effect?
choices: The intensity of the incident light
The frequency of the incident light
The distance of the light source from the emitter
The material of the collector plate
questions.solution: The frequency of the incident light determines the energy of individual photons, which directly affects the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons. Higher frequency means higher photon energy, leading to greater kinetic energy in the electrons. Intensity affects the number of electrons emitted, not their energy. The distance of the light source and the material of the collector plate do not influence the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons.

questions.stem: If a metal plate is illuminated with light of frequency below the threshold frequency, what happens to the photoelectric current?
questions.solution: If the frequency of the light is below the threshold frequency, the energy of the photons is insufficient to eject electrons from the metal, so no photoelectric current is produced. The current being zero is the only possible outcome in this case. Options suggesting the current increases or decreases with frequency or intensity are incorrect because they apply when the frequency is above the threshold.

questions.stem: If the frequency of incident light is increased while keeping the intensity constant, what happens to the stopping potential?
questions.solution: The stopping potential increases because higher frequency light provides more energy to the photoelectrons, giving them greater kinetic energy. This requires a higher retarding potential to stop them. Intensity affects the number of electrons, not their maximum kinetic energy, so it does not influence the stopping potential.

questions.stem: A metal surface is illuminated by light of frequency higher than the threshold frequency. If the intensity of the light is increased, what happens to the number of photoelectrons emitted per second?
questions.solution: When the frequency of light is above the threshold, increasing the intensity means more photons are incident on the metal surface. Each photon can eject one electron if it has enough energy, so more photons lead to more electrons being emitted. The correct option is that the number of photoelectrons increases. The other options are incorrect because they do not align with the relationship between light intensity and electron emission in the photoelectric effect.

questions.stem: Why is the de Broglie wavelength of macroscopic objects not measurable?
choices: Because their momentum is too large
Because their mass is too small
Because they do not have any wave-like properties
Because they are not affected by electromagnetic radiation
questions.solution: The de Broglie wavelength is inversely proportional to momentum, and macroscopic objects have very large momenta due to their significant mass and velocity, making their wavelengths too small to measure. The other options are incorrect because mass being small would not explain the lack of measurable wavelength, wave-like properties exist for all matter regardless of size, and electromagnetic radiation does not directly affect the measurement of wavelength.
